name: India
hook: Gandhi, the Ganges and Sanskrit: the clues keep returning to a small set of names and rivers.

facts.label: Mahatma Gandhi
facts.statement: Mohandas "Mahatma" Gandhi, called the "Great Soul," led India's nonviolent independence movement and after 1915 left India only once, to visit London.

facts.label: the Ganges
facts.statement: The Ganges, India's most sacred river, is named for a Hindu goddess; Allahabad sits at its junction with the Yamuna.

facts.label: Sanskrit
facts.statement: Sanskrit, the ancient language of India related to Greek and Latin, is the language of the Mahabharata's 100,000 verses.

facts.label: Vasco da Gama
facts.statement: Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498, became viceroy of Portuguese India, and died at Cochin in 1524.

facts.label: Indira Gandhi
facts.statement: Indira Gandhi became India's first woman prime minister and the "Madam P.M." of the Congress-I era; a Rajasthan canal is named for her.

facts.label: Calcutta
facts.statement: Calcutta, now Kolkata, is the cultural center of eastern India and was the world's jute-processing capital around 1900.

facts.label: India's population
facts.statement: India is projected to have more people than China by 2100 and has the world's highest share of vegetarians, about 38%.
